claims.claim: KNI-272, a peptidomimetic HIV protease inhibitor structurally related to the query, had absolute oral bioavailability of 36.4% when given as a capsule post-prandially in patients, directly supporting F≥20% for the query under fed conditions.
Atazanavir, an HIV protease inhibitor, has oral bioavailability >90% when taken with food, providing additional fed-state class-level support for high F.
Paritaprevir, a protease inhibitor, had absolute oral bioavailability of 52.6% from a tablet, further supporting high F for peptidomimetic protease inhibitors.

The poor-bioavailability contexts (danavorexton, argatroban, rifampin-induced propafenone) are structurally and conditionally distant from the query and do not outweigh the fed-state HIV protease inhibitor evidence.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for nelfinavir itself is present in the supplied records.
KNI-272 fed-state F is based on only n=2 patients.
Atazanavir bioavailability type is unspecified and lacks dose/formulation details.
Query-specific fed-state solubility, permeability, and first-pass metabolism are not directly measured.
content.decision_summary: High is supported: the query is a peptidomimetic HIV protease inhibitor under fed conditions, and the closest transferable contexts (KNI-272 postprandial F 36.4%; atazanavir with food >90%) affirm F≥20%; distant poor-bioavailability contexts do not override this.
